02 · Differential expression

Load packages

pacman::p_load(here, limpa, limma, dplyr, ggplot2, purrr, tibble, tidyr, writexl)
here::i_am("02_Differential_Expression/02_Differential/a_script/02_differential.qmd")

Read proteins and design

proteins holds the normalised log2 abundances and their standard errors; d holds the design, the contrasts and the baseline contrast’s name. Design rows and matrix columns must name the same samples in the same order; equal dimensions alone would not catch a swapped sample.

proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
fitted_slope_file <- here(
  "01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "quant_runs", "proteins_slope_fitted.rds"
)

stopifnot(identical(rownames(d$design), colnames(proteins$E)))

Fit

limpa’s sequence is dpcDE(), contrasts.fit(), eBayes(), topTable(). dpcDE() takes the place of lmFit() because only it reads the standard errors from dpcQuant(), as precision weights. No per-sample quality weights (limpa’s default): estimated, they ranged from 0.09 to 3.6 and did not follow contaminant load. contrasts.fit() forms the five comparisons and eBayes() moderates each protein’s variance toward a prior fitted across all proteins; robust = TRUE keeps proteins with outlying variances from distorting that prior. The design carries the blood index, and its coefficient, read before the contrasts are formed, is each protein’s blood slope: log2 protein per log2 haemoglobin, near 1 for a protein that comes only from blood and near 0 for one blood does not carry.

coefficient_fit <- dpcDE(proteins, d$design)
blood_fit <- topTable(eBayes(coefficient_fit, robust = TRUE), coef = "blood", number = Inf,
  sort.by = "none")
fit <- eBayes(contrasts.fit(coefficient_fit, d$contrasts), robust = TRUE)
sum(blood_fit$adj.P.Val < 0.05)
[1] 951

Results

In topTable(), sort.by = "none" keeps protein order (the default sorts on the B statistic). Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjustment controls the false discovery rate within each contrast, not across all five.

results <- map(colnames(d$contrasts), function(cn) {
  topTable(fit, coef = cn, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") |>
    rownames_to_column("protein") |>
    mutate(contrast = cn, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

contrast_summary <- results |>
  summarise(
    n_tested = n(),
    n_fdr_05 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05),
    n_fdr_10 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.10),
    min_adj_p = min(adj.P.Val),
    .by = contrast
  )
contrast_summary |>
  mutate(min_adj_p = signif(min_adj_p, 3))
                     contrast n_tested n_fdr_05 n_fdr_10 min_adj_p
1                BFR_Post-Pre     3042       95      170  1.52e-04
2               HLRT_Post-Pre     3042      218      332  2.16e-10
3            BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre     3042        0        0  4.21e-01
4          BFR_Post-HLRT_Post     3042        0        0  4.53e-01
5 Modality_x_Time_Interaction     3042        0        0  6.82e-01

Inspect p-value distributions

Per contrast: the estimated share of true nulls (propTrueNull()), the median absolute t and the fraction of p below 0.2. Under a flat null, 20% of p fall below 0.2 and the median |t| is about 0.67.

null_summary <- results |>
  summarise(
    prop_true_null = round(propTrueNull(P.Value), 3),
    median_abs_t = round(median(abs(t)), 3),
    p_below_0.2 = round(mean(P.Value < 0.2), 3), .by = contrast
  )
null_summary
                     contrast prop_true_null median_abs_t p_below_0.2
1                BFR_Post-Pre          0.797        0.932       0.349
2               HLRT_Post-Pre          0.733        1.041       0.417
3            BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre          0.957        0.733       0.234
4          BFR_Post-HLRT_Post          0.970        0.718       0.224
5 Modality_x_Time_Interaction          0.999        0.671       0.191

The dashed line is the count per bin if p-values were uniform.

ggplot(results, aes(P.Value)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, fill = "grey35") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(proteins) / 20, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~contrast) +
  labs(x = "p", y = "proteins", caption = "dashed line marks a flat null") +
  theme_minimal()

From the fitted standard errors, the interaction effect each protein would need for 80% power at an unadjusted two-sided 0.05 threshold, on the log2 scale: median and 90th percentile across proteins. It describes sensitivity, not FDR-adjusted power.

se <- fit$stdev.unscaled[, "Modality_x_Time_Interaction"] * sqrt(fit$s2.post)
round(quantile(se * (qt(0.975, fit$df.total) + qt(0.80, fit$df.total)), c(0.5, 0.9)), 3)
  50%   90% 
0.490 0.824

The pi score

pi_score is P.Value^abs(logFC), which equals 10 to the minus Xiao et al.’s π (|logFC| times −log10 p; 2014, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btr671), so it orders proteins as π does, smallest first: large effects with small p. It ranks the two within-leg contrasts, controls no error rate and selects nothing. The mean number of observed precursors per sample sits beside it, because the top of a pi ranking is often thinly observed.

results |>
  filter(contrast %in% c("BFR_Post-Pre", "HLRT_Post-Pre")) |>
  mutate(pi_score = P.Value^abs(logFC)) |>
  slice_min(pi_score, n = 10, by = contrast) |>
  mutate(mean_obs = round(rowMeans(proteins$other$n.observations)[protein], 2)) |>
  select(contrast, protein, Genes, logFC, adj.P.Val, pi_score, NPrec, mean_obs)

Baseline comparison

The two legs before training, where counterbalanced legs should differ by nothing; a difference can be biological or technical. The five smallest p:

baseline <- filter(results, contrast == d$baseline)
stopifnot(nrow(baseline) == nrow(proteins))

slice_min(baseline, P.Value, n = 5) |>
  select(protein, Genes, logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val)

Without the blood covariate

The same fit without the blood index, its BH discoveries per contrast beside the primary fit’s.

unadjusted_design <- d$design[, colnames(d$design) != "blood"]
unadjusted <- dpcDE(proteins, unadjusted_design, plot = FALSE) |>
  contrasts.fit(d$contrasts[colnames(unadjusted_design), ]) |>
  eBayes(robust = TRUE)
primary_hits <- decideTests(fit) != 0
unadjusted_hits <- decideTests(unadjusted) != 0
contrast_summary$n_fdr_05_unadjusted <- colSums(unadjusted_hits)[contrast_summary$contrast]
rbind(
  blood_adjusted = colSums(primary_hits),
  unadjusted = colSums(unadjusted_hits),
  both = colSums(primary_hits & unadjusted_hits)
)
               BFR_Post-Pre HLRT_Post-Pre BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre BFR_Post-HLRT_Post
blood_adjusted           95           218                0                  0
unadjusted               86           161                0                  0
both                     86           153                0                  0
               Modality_x_Time_Interaction

unadjusted                               0
both                                     0

Slope sensitivity

02_quantify_run.R --sensitivity also quantifies with the detection-curve (DPC) slope fitted to these data (0.478) instead of the preset 0.7. When that run exists, it gets the same detection filter, normalisation and design, and its discovery counts are set beside the primary run’s.

fitted_slope <- readRDS(fitted_slope_file)
fitted_slope <- fitted_slope[
  filterByDetection(fitted_slope, n.samples = min(table(fitted_slope$targets$group))),
]
fitted_slope$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(fitted_slope$E, method = "cyclicloess")
stopifnot(identical(colnames(fitted_slope$E), rownames(d$design)))
refit <- dpcDE(fitted_slope, d$design, plot = FALSE) |>
  contrasts.fit(d$contrasts) |>
  eBayes(robust = TRUE)
stopifnot(all(rownames(primary_hits) %in% rownames(refit)))
refit_hits <- decideTests(refit)[rownames(primary_hits), , drop = FALSE] != 0
rbind(
  slope_0.7 = colSums(primary_hits),
  fitted_curve = colSums(refit_hits),
  both = colSums(primary_hits & refit_hits)
)
             BFR_Post-Pre HLRT_Post-Pre BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre BFR_Post-HLRT_Post
slope_0.7              95           218                0                  0
fitted_curve          100           221                0                  0
both                   84           200                0                  0
             Modality_x_Time_Interaction

fitted_curve                           0
both                                   0

Save results

fit.rds keeps the fitted model for the stages that rebuild contrasts. 02_differential.xlsx holds DEP_matrix (one row per protein: log2 fold change, p and BH-adjusted p per contrast, and the blood slope with its BH-adjusted p), discovery counts with and without the blood covariate, and the distribution summaries.

dep_matrix <- results |>
  select(protein, Genes, NPrec, contrast, logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = contrast,
    values_from = c(logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val),
    names_glue = "{contrast}_{.value}"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    blood_slope = blood_fit[protein, "logFC"],
    blood_adj.P.Val = blood_fit[protein, "adj.P.Val"]
  )

out <- here("02_Differential_Expression", "02_Differential", "c_data")
saveRDS(fit, file.path(out, "fit.rds"))
write_xlsx(
  list(
    DEP_matrix = dep_matrix,
    contrast_summary = contrast_summary,
    null_summary = null_summary
  ),
  file.path(out, "02_differential.xlsx")
)
